title: Files and formats
overview_markdown:
**What you will do.** You will check the files that the laboratory sent. You will convert them to the format of [PLINK 2](../docs/glossary.md#plink-2), the free program used throughout this course. Then you will correct [strand](../docs/glossary.md#strand) differences, add disease and age information, and save a first [checkpoint](../docs/glossary.md#checkpoint).

**What you will learn.**

- What the [genotype](../docs/glossary.md#genotype) files contain and why they must stay together.
- How to measure [missingness](../docs/glossary.md#missingness), the share of genotypes that could not be read.
- Why some variants cannot be oriented to a strand.
- What a [genome build](../docs/glossary.md#genome-build) is and why GRCh37 and GRCh38 must not be mixed.
- How to join disease and age to the right person.

**How long it takes.** About 60 minutes. Steps 2.5 and 2.6 take the longest, because they introduce new ideas.
recap_markdown:
- You checked that the laboratory export has 2,016 sample wells and 299,523 variant entries.
- You converted the BED, BIM and FAM files to PGEN, PVAR and PSAM without losing any sample or variant.
- You measured missingness for samples and for variants, and removed nothing yet.
- You flipped 400 sites and excluded 3,013 sites, leaving 296,510 variants.
- You lifted a 10,000-site GRCh37 exercise to GRCh38: 9,970 sites stayed on the same chromosome, and eight mapped to the reverse strand.
- You added Disease, age and recorded sex to the 2,016 wells and saved the 2.8 checkpoint.

**Next:** module 3 cleans the samples: low call rate, sex check, heterozygosity, relatives, duplicates and batch effects.
